answer: Like a falcon that only hunts in a known territory, an agent economy can grant trading rights only after an agent proves sustained useful work over time: each identity accrues reputation slowly through completed jobs verified by independent peers, and that reputation decays when idle. A fake identity starts with zero standing in the tundra of the market and must earn trust one job at a time, like a cedar adding one ring per season. An attacker would have to fund real work for every fake identity, making a Sybil flood more expensive than any gain from it.
